title: fix: preserve ownership when exporting keep-id containers
body:
Fixes #29856

Rootless containers created with `--userns=keep-id` store host-mapped IDs in their mounted root filesystem. `podman export` passed no archive ID mappings, so exported tar headers exposed those host IDs instead of the container ownership. This caused files owned by container UID/GID 1000 to be exported as 0/0.

Pass the container's configured UID/GID mappings to the archive tar operation so headers are converted back to container IDs. Add a rootless `--userns=keep-id` end-to-end regression test that checks the exported tar header.

Tests:
- `make podman`
- `go test ./libpod -run ^$`
- `go test ./test/e2e -run ^$`
- Rootless Linux Ginkgo E2E: `podman export preserves ownership with keep-id user namespaces` (1 passed)
- Manual baseline comparison: 0/0 before the change, 1000/1000 after the change

Thanks @Honny1! `Fixes: #29856` is in the commit message now (the commit got rewritten for the sign-off change as well).

Regarding the e2e test: the PR already adds one in `test/e2e/export_test.go` — "podman export preserves ownership with keep-id user namespaces". It creates a container with `--userns=keep-id`, creates a file owned by 1000:1000, exports it, and asserts the tar header carries 1000/1000 instead of the host-mapped ID — the same bug and the same export code path as the reproducer in the issue, with the header check being the equivalent of the `tar tv` listing there.

If you'd rather have the test mirror the reproducer literally (image with a dedicated user, create + export without starting, check `/home/user`), I'm happy to rework it.
